title: Object-Oriented Programming: Modeling the World in Objects

questions.question: What is the core shift from procedural to object-oriented programming?
options: Replacing all functions with global variables
Bundling data with the code allowed to touch it, so each object guards its own state
Removing data from programs entirely
Writing code only in assembly language
questions.rationale: OOP flips the procedural layout: instead of free functions touching shared data, each object encapsulates its state and exposes a small set of operations.

questions.question: The real purpose of encapsulation is best stated as:
options: Making code run faster by hiding variables
Encrypting all object data
Protecting invariants by making fields private and reachable only through methods
Preventing objects from being copied
questions.rationale: Encapsulation is not secrecy but safety: with the balance reachable only through deposit(), no stray code can ever set it to −500 — the invariant cannot break.

questions.question: `ElectricCar extends Vehicle` is an example of which relationship, and what does it provide?
options: Composition — reuse by storing an engine
Inheritance — an is-a relationship that reuses the parent's fields and methods
Polymorphism — the same call with many behaviors
Encapsulation — hiding the battery
questions.rationale: Inheritance is the is-a relationship: an ElectricCar is a Vehicle plus extras, and code written for Vehicle works on it for free — though deep hierarchies risk fragility.

questions.question: A loop calls describe() on a list containing different Vehicle subclasses, and each answers differently. This is:
options: Overloading
Encapsulation
Polymorphism via method overriding
Dependency inversion
questions.rationale: Polymorphism lets the same call invoke each receiver's own override of the method; the loop neither knows nor cares which subclass it holds.

questions.question: What is the difference between overriding and overloading?
options: Overriding redefines an inherited method in a subclass; overloading uses one name with different parameter lists in the same class
They are synonyms
Overloading only works in Python; overriding only in JavaScript
Overriding happens at compile time; both remove methods
questions.rationale: Overriding redefines an inherited method at run time; overloading is a compile-time idea — same method name, different parameter lists.

questions.question: Why does the lesson recommend composition (has-a) over inheritance (is-a) in many cases?
options: Composition always runs faster
Because inheritance is deprecated in all modern languages
Inheritance hierarchies are fragile — parent changes ripple into children — so has-a wiring is often safer
Composition forbids objects from having methods
questions.rationale: A change to a parent class ripples into every descendant; a Car having an Engine avoids that fragility, so 'has-a' is preferred unless the is-a hierarchy is genuinely true and stable.

questions.question: In the SOLID principles, what does the 'O' stand for?
options: Objectivity — every class must inherit Object
Open/closed — open for extension, closed for modification
Ownership — one owner per class
Optimization — profile before designing
questions.rationale: O is the open/closed principle: extend behavior by adding new code (e.g., new subclasses), not by editing existing, working classes.

questions.question: In the JavaScript example, `super(make, 0)` inside ElectricCar's constructor does what?
options: Creates a new Vehicle object unrelated to this one
Calls the parent Vehicle constructor to initialize the inherited fields
Clones the parent class
Marks the method as private
questions.rationale: super() invokes the parent class's constructor so the inherited fields (make, speed) are initialized before the subclass adds its own (battery).

questions.question: A single class that 'knows everything' and keeps growing is an example of which pitfall, and what is the cure?
options: The God object; split it by responsibility
Deep fragile hierarchy; flatten it
Tight coupling; add more interfaces
Primitive obsession; add more fields
questions.rationale: The God object concentrates every responsibility in one class; the cure is splitting it by responsibility (the single-responsibility principle).

questions.question: Which statement best captures the lesson's verdict on OOP versus functional programming?
options: Functional programming replaces OOP everywhere
They are enemies and only one may be used per project
They are not enemies: modern code mixes state-in-objects with pure functions
OOP has no state at all
questions.rationale: OOP bundles state with behavior while functional keeps data immutable and functions pure — modern JavaScript, Python, and Java programs mix both freely.
